properties.description:
THREE THINGS, and the corpus had two of them while authors wrote all three into one. `name` is what a list renders; `description` is what the check IS; `findings` (new) is what a RUN found. `add_verification` gains `description`; `set_verification_status` gains `findings`; `loop_status`'s rollup shortens a long name AND says that it did. (The guard matched the OBSERVATION that named this defect and the REQUIREMENT that answers it; this is the built thing that closes both.)

⭐⭐ THE REQUIREMENT NAMED ITS OWN PRECONDITION AND THE ANSWER WAS NO. It asked, in its own words: "THE LOAD-BEARING UNCERTAINTY, to answer BEFORE building: WOULD A NEW FIELD ALONE CHANGE ANYTHING? A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is." Measured before writing any code:

    Verifications                        164
    median `name`                         76 words   (72 over 100, 17 over 300, longest 654)
    `description` — DECLARED, fulltext,
    and the node's EMBEDDING FIELD         1 use in 164

⇒ SO A `findings` FIELD ALONE WOULD HAVE BECOME THE SECOND UNUSED FIELD. The uncertainty was real and the answer sat in the corpus for anyone who counted.

⭐ AND THE ROOT CAUSE WAS REACHABILITY, NOT NEGLECT — found by reading the constructor rather than inferring from the number. `add_verification(id, name, method, level)` HAD NO PARAMETER FOR `description`. The only route was raw `create_node` and essentially nobody took it. Authors wrote reports into `name` because **`name` was the only string the constructor accepted**. The field was not ignored; it was unwritable. That is `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` one door along — there, 112 nodes wrote an UNDECLARED property because the declared route did not fit; here, one node wrote a declared property because the route did not exist.

WHERE EACH FIELD IS WRITTEN IS THE DESIGN, not a convenience:
• `description` on the CONSTRUCTOR — what the check is, stated once.
• `findings` on `set_verification_status` — what a RUN found, restated whenever an outcome changes. Evidence belongs to a run, so it is recorded when the run produces it, by the caller holding it.
• Omitting `findings` LEAVES IT ALONE, exactly as `last_run_at` does since 2026-08-08 — re-marking a check passing without restating evidence must not erase it. Erasing is a deliberate act deserving an explicit one, the convention `set_interface_spec`, `set_decision_status` and `set_epoch_status` all state and which this function's own first line already promised.

THE ROLLUP, their second ask: `loop_status`'s `verifications.attention[]` shortens a `name` past 25 words — and carries `name_truncated`, `name_words`, and a top-level `names_truncated` note saying how many and where the full text is. ⭐ THE ANNOUNCEMENT IS THE POINT, not decoration: a silently shortened name reads as "that is the whole name", a vacuous zero one layer over, and it is the SIXTH of Anthony's own engineering principles — no silent caps or truncation. Truncating without fixing reachability would have been the stopgap `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` forbids; cause and symptom were fixed together.

⚠️ BOUNDS, stated rather than discovered later:
• NOTHING IS MIGRATED. The 164 existing long names stay as they are. A property once written cannot be removed, so the best available repair would duplicate rather than move — and rewriting 164 authored names is not a mechanical act. New checks get the shape; old ones keep theirs. The median will fall slowly or not at all, and that is honest rather than disappointing.
• `findings` IS NOT VALIDATED OR PARSED. reflow2 records what an author says a run found and never judges it (`dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful`). A `passing` status beside findings describing a failure is a contradiction only a reader can catch — dev_storyflow's 2026-08-07 report exactly, where a check recorded "EXIT 0, verdict STALE" and stayed passing forever. This gives that evidence a home; it does not make the contradiction computable.
• The schema gains a PROPERTY, not a type, so the version stamp (counting node/edge types, 29/61) does not move and an older reflow2 can still read the graph.
properties.name: A check records what it FOUND separately from what it IS, and the rollup that made a cheap call expensive to read says when it shortened a name
